intro: You've searched for a business solicitor near you, which usually means something concrete has come up in your company or trading life and you want someone local who can take it on. Perhaps you're setting up a limited company, signing a lease, or dealing with a contract that has gone wrong. We introduce you to a suitable UK solicitor who quotes you directly, so you can compare what's on offer before deciding.
need_heading: What people searching for a business solicitor near me usually need
need_lead: Most enquiries come from owners and directors who want practical legal help with the commercial side of running a business.
needs: You are forming a limited company and want the paperwork, including a shareholder agreement, set up properly from the start.
A customer or supplier has broken the terms of a contract and you need to know where you stand before things escalate.
You are taking on commercial premises and want a solicitor to look over the lease before you sign.
You need employment contracts, policies or advice on handling a staffing issue in line with UK employment law.
You are buying or selling a business, or bringing in a new shareholder, and want the documents handled carefully.
context_heading: Checking who will actually handle your matter
context: Solicitors in England and Wales are regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA), and you can check an individual or firm on the SRA's register. In Scotland the regulator is the Law Society of Scotland, and in Northern Ireland it is the Law Society of Northern Ireland. Regulated firms must hold professional indemnity insurance and have a complaints procedure, and if a service complaint is not resolved, the Legal Ombudsman can look at it in England and Wales.

The word "lawyer" is not protected on its own, so it is worth confirming that whoever handles your matter is a solicitor, a chartered legal executive (CILEx) or another authorised professional. Reserved activities such as conducting court litigation and certain probate and conveyancing work can only be carried out by authorised people. Asking this early saves confusion later.
tell_heading: What to tell us when you enquire
tell: Describe your business, including what it does and how it is structured, whether that is a sole trader, partnership or limited company.
Explain the specific issue or task, such as a contract dispute, a lease, company formation or an employment question.
Say what stage you are at, for example whether documents have been signed, a deadline is approaching or a dispute has just arisen.
Mention any relevant dates, such as a completion date or a response deadline, so the solicitor knows how urgent it is.
Say where you are based and how far you are willing to travel, since you searched for a solicitor near you.
Note whether you would prefer to deal with things in person, by phone or by email, and whether you have a budget in mind.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the business solicitor
questions: Are you regulated by the SRA, the Law Society of Scotland or the Law Society of Northern Ireland, and can you confirm who will handle my matter?
What experience do you have with the kind of business issue I have described?
How will you charge for this work, and can you give me an estimate or a fixed fee before we start?
What do you need from me, and are there any deadlines I should be aware of?
Will you keep me updated as the matter progresses, and how often?
If I am unhappy with the service, what is your complaints procedure?

faqs.q: Do I need a solicitor who is local to my business?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Many business matters can be handled by phone, email and video call, but meeting in person can help with complex documents or disputes. If you searched for a solicitor near you, tell us how far you are willing to travel and we can introduce you to someone suitable.

faqs.q: Can a business solicitor help with a shareholder agreement?
faqs.a: Yes. Business solicitors commonly draft and prepare shareholder agreements, which set out how a company is run and what happens if shareholders disagree or one wants to leave. Getting this right early can prevent costly disputes later.

faqs.q: How do I check that a solicitor is properly regulated?
faqs.a: In England and Wales you can check an individual or firm on the SRA's register. In Scotland, check with the Law Society of Scotland, and in Northern Ireland with the Law Society of Northern Ireland. Regulated firms must also hold professional indemnity insurance and have a complaints procedure.

faqs.q: What should I have ready before I speak to a business solicitor?
faqs.a: Gather any relevant contracts, correspondence, company documents and a clear summary of what you need help with. Knowing your key dates and what outcome you want helps the solicitor quote accurately. You can include these details in your enquiry to us.

extra_heading: Comparing business solicitors close to you
extra: Searching for a business solicitor near you often means you want the option of sitting down together with your paperwork, rather than handling everything at a distance. That can matter when you are going through a lease clause by clause or explaining how your company actually works. Plenty of commercial matters are dealt with perfectly well by phone and email, so think about how much face-to-face contact you genuinely need before you narrow your list by distance.

When you weigh up the solicitors you hear back from, compare like with like. Check that the person quoting is regulated to do the specific work you need, ask whether the quote covers the whole matter or only part of it, and find out what happens if the job turns out to be bigger than expected. A clear explanation of how the fee is built up tells you more than a single figure ever could.

It also helps to ask what the solicitor would need from you before any work starts, and roughly what the process looks like from there. Business matters often turn on documents you already hold, such as signed contracts, board minutes or correspondence with a customer or supplier. Being ready with those shortens the first conversation and makes any quote more reliable.

extra_faqs.q: Should I choose a business solicitor in my own town?
extra_faqs.a: It depends on the matter. Company formation, contract drafting and employment documents are usually handled comfortably by phone and email, while a lease, a dispute or a sale of the business may benefit from meeting in person. Tell us how far you are willing to travel and we can take that into account when introducing you to a solicitor.

extra_faqs.q: What is the difference between a business solicitor and a general practice solicitor?
extra_faqs.a: A general practice solicitor may take on a wide range of personal and commercial work, whereas a business solicitor concentrates on companies, contracts, disputes, employment and commercial property. Ask what proportion of their work is commercial, and whether they have dealt with an issue like yours before, so you can judge the fit for yourself.

extra_faqs.q: Will the first conversation cost me anything?
extra_faqs.a: That varies between firms, so ask before you book. Some solicitors offer a short initial conversation at no charge, while others charge for their time from the outset. Whatever the answer, get it in writing along with an estimate of the likely cost of the whole matter before you instruct anyone.
